title: Renewal Signal Matrix and KPI Index — draft
content:
Purpose:
This working doc is a compact, operational playbook for the Customer Success (CS) team to use when preparing renewal conversations and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs). It focuses on the key technical signals that most strongly correlate with renewal risk for infra-sensitive customers: latency, uptime, cost-per-token, and cache hit rate. The goal is a consistent signal matrix + short runbooks so CSMs and Solutions Engineers (SEs) can diagnose issues quickly and present quantitative remediation steps in renewal decks.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: CSMs, SEs, renewal leads, product ops.
- Scope: definitions, measurement points, alert thresholds, sample KPI table, and lightweight playbook actions for common signal failures.

Quick glossary (why these matter for renewal):
- Latency: customer-facing delay drives user frustration and product abandonment; also strongly influences perceived value in real-time UIs.
- Uptime: availability is a basic SLA expectation; intermittent outages increase churn risk.
- Cost-per-token: affects economic viability for customers; sudden cost increases are renewal blockers.
- Cache hit rate: high-value optimization lever; low hit rates usually mean unnecessary compute spend and higher tail latency.

Metric definitions and measurement guidance:
1) Latency (API-level, per-route)
   - Definition: end-to-end response time from request ingress at Redwood API gateway to final token emitted (includes pre-processing, model runtime, post-processing). Measured percentiles: p50, p90, p95, p99.
   - Measurement points: per-route (customer route), per-model-version, and global (all traffic). Use p90 and p99 for alerts; p50 for trend monitoring.
   - Unit: milliseconds (ms).
   - Collection frequency: 1m buckets aggregated to hourly/day for reporting.
   - Notes: distinguish server-side model generation time (inference) vs client-side network overhead. When possible, present both gateway-to-gateway and model-runtime-only numbers.

2) Uptime (availability)
   - Definition: percentage of successful requests (HTTP 2xx/3xx) vs total requests over the measurement window, excluding scheduled maintenance windows.
   - SLA framing: e.g., 99.9% monthly for enterprise customers.
   - Measurement window: 30-day rolling (also show 7-day for emergent issues).
   - Incident attribution: annotate outages by root cause (region, model, routing policy, infra).

3) Cost-per-token (effective cost)
   - Definition: an estimate of the customer-facing per-token cost derived from Redwood’s infra cost allocation plus model licensing/variant differentials where applicable. (This is a derived internal metric for CS conversations — not a bill line item.)
   - Formula (simplified): cost_per_token = (compute_cost_allocated + network_cost_allocated + storage_cost_allocated + licensing_cost) / billed_tokens.
   - Common simplifications: for most quick QBRs, use compute + model licensing divided by tokens; call out caching savings separately.
   - Unit: USD per 1k tokens (or USD per token, whichever the customer prefers).

4) Cache hit rate (prefix / KV / inference cache)
   - Definition: proportion of requests served from cache (prefix & KV caching) vs total requests that otherwise would need a full model forward.
   - Formula: cache_hit_rate = cached_responses / total_cacheable_requests.
   - Measurement nuance: some requests are intentionally uncacheable (high-entropy prompts); always show numerator and denominator.
   - Impact: higher cache hit reduces both latency and cost.

Signal matrix and alert guidance (short):
- Latency p95 > target for 3+ hours (persistent): Severity = high -> notify SE + infra + assign incident lead. Short-term actions: check burst capacity, routing fallbacks, and per-model A/B fallback to faster variant.
- Uptime < SLA for 24h window or >1 rolling-day outage incident: Severity = critical -> full incident playbook, customer escalation prep.
- Cost-per-token increases >25% month-over-month (persistent for billing period): Severity = medium-high -> analyze model variant usage, quantization/instance sizing recommendations, caching opportunities.
- Cache hit rate < expected baseline (customer baseline) and leading to >10% cost delta: Severity = medium -> audit prompt patterns, suggest prefixing and caching policies, tune TTLs.

Sample KPI table (compact):
Columns: metric | preferred unit | enterprise target | mid-market target | alert threshold | owner | cadence
- Latency p95 | ms | <= 450 ms | <= 650 ms | > 900 ms (2h sustained) | infra/SE | hourly/daily
- Latency p99 | ms | <= 900 ms | <= 1200 ms | > 1800 ms (1h spike) | infra/SE | hourly
- Uptime (30d rolling) | % | >= 99.9 | >= 99.5 | < 99.0 | SRE/CS ops | daily/weekly
- Cost-per-1k-tokens | USD | <= $2.50 | <= $3.50 | > +25% MoM | finance + CS | monthly
- Cache hit rate | % | >= 65% | >= 40% | < 25% | SE + CS | daily/weekly

Renewal Health Index (working model) — weighted score used on renewal decks
- Signals and weights (example):
  - Uptime (30d): 30% weight (score 0-100 based on distance to SLA)
  - Latency experience (p95/p99 combined): 25% weight
  - Cost stability (cost-per-token trend): 20% weight
  - Cache effectiveness (hit rate and savings): 15% weight
  - Support/incident responsiveness (CS qualitative): 10% weight
- Example scoring (enterprise customer): uptime = 99.95 -> score 95; latency = near-target -> score 85; cost-per-token +5% -> score 80; cache hit 70% -> score 90; CS NPS input 80 -> score 80. Weighted composite ~86 -> "Green" renewal conversation.

Mini runbooks (quick triage steps per common failure):
- High latency, normal uptime:
  1) Check per-route p95/p99 — is it isolated to one route/model?
  2) Inspect model variant and sequence length distribution (long prompts cause tail latency).
  3) If tail is high, enable faster model fallback for the route OR enable dynamic batching adjustments.
  4) Communicate to customer: temporary fallback plan + expected impact on quality.

- Rising cost-per-token:
  1) Pull last 3 months token breakdown by model/version and by route.
  2) Identify uncacheable routes and large prompt generators.
  3) Recommend: enable prefix caching on predictable flows, quantized variant for low-sensitivity flows, or reserved capacity sizing changes.
  4) Prepare a cost-savings estimate (dollars/month) for the QBR.

- Low cache hit rate:
  1) Confirm what fraction of total requests were flagged as cacheable in logs.
  2) Review prompt templates; propose canonicalization and TTL adjustments.
  3) Pilot pre-warming for frequently-used prefixes.

Customer-facing artifacts to prepare for renewal QBR (deliverables checklist):
- 1-page Renewal Health index (visual score + top 3 actions)
- Short technical appendix: recent incidents, model-variant usage, cost delta table
- Cost-saving proposals: conservative and aggressive (with estimated USD/month)
- Action plan for next 90 days with owners and SLAs

Reporting templates (copyable snippets for decks):
- KPI snapshot card (1 slide): show last 30d uptime, p95 latency, cost/1k tokens trend, cache hit rate, Renewal Health score.
- Incident impact table: date, root cause, minutes of customer impact, mitigation, permanent fix status.

Open questions / TODOs (for CS + Product):
- Agree on a standard cost-per-token calculation that is defensible in customer conversations (finance + product to finalize).
- Decide canonical tiers and target thresholds for mid-market vs enterprise (product ops).
- Create automated deck generator that pulls 30d windows for the above metrics (product + analytics).

Appendix: sample numeric targets by customer tier (example quick reference)
- Self-serve: p95 <= 800ms, uptime >= 99.5%, cost/1k <= $4.50, cache >= 35%
- Mid-market: p95 <= 650ms, uptime >= 99.5%, cost/1k <= $3.50, cache >= 40%
- Enterprise: p95 <= 450ms, uptime >= 99.9%, cost/1k <= $2.50, cache >= 65%

Notes to reviewer:
- This is a compact, operational-first doc intended to be copied into QBR slides and customer emails. Please flag: missing definitions, better calculation for cost allocation, or missing owner mappings.
- If we lock on the cost-per-token formula, we should add a short script (SQL + lightweight python) to auto-generate the cost table per customer for the last 90 days.

End of draft.
